ok-seb-2026-runoff-results.title: Official results, Runoff Primary Election, August 25, 2026: state officers, State Senator, State Representative, District Judge, Associate District Judge, District Attorney, county officers and city contests
ok-seb-2026-runoff-results.note: The Board's results site marked these results Official when its two export files were saved through a browser on 2026-10-03 (the site refuses scripts): one row per candidate per contest, and the same county by county (SHA-256 of the county file 48cb3c7af97b0b0f70dbb780aac9e974d5127815859a29c42f777e3519623b58). Read by heading: the office, party, the county or city holding it, precincts, each candidate's name and votes. 19 contests for the state races' primary fields and 26 for county offices, district attorneys and the first rounds of city contests on the November list, each placed by its office, county, district or city and ward; checked: every precinct reporting, each candidate's absentee, early and election-day votes adding up to the total, and each contest's total and each candidate's equal to the sum of the county rows (all agree). Names are printed in capitals and paired with the names already loaded, whose spelling is kept; other names are shown in ordinary capitals. Not loaded: the questions and propositions, and the city, town and school contests decided before November (see the gaps).

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 every Oklahoma county elects a county assessor, a county treasurer and the county commissioners for Districts 1 and 3, by party; the county clerk, court clerk, sheriff and District 2 commissioner are elected in 2028. Fire protection districts elect board members each November, without parties, and Bartlesville, Clinton, El Reno, Lawton, Tulsa and Yukon have city contests on this ballot. Most other cities and towns elect in April of odd-numbered years (a city with its own charter may choose another date), and school boards were elected on February 10 and April 7, 2026.
local_calendar.s: 19 O.S. 131 (county officers) and 901.5 (fire protection districts); 11 O.S. 16-102 and 16-103 (cities and towns); Oklahoma State Election Board, 2026 Voter Information Calendar (school board election dates)

local_coverage.t: From the State Election Board's November 3 list, read county by county for all 77 counties: every contest it prints for a county office, a city or town office or a fire protection district board (41 contests, 88 candidates, in 28 counties). Oklahoma prints only contested races. From the Board's official results of the June 16 primary and the August 25 runoff: the party primaries of the county contests on the November list and the first rounds of its city contests, with their votes, and 99 county seats the November list does not print, settled in a primary or a runoff and shown with their winners. An office with one candidate left appears in no list or result and is not shown; no district attorney is on the November list (of the 27 offices, 23 had one candidate when filing closed and 4 had candidates of one party only; the four decided in the June 16 primary are shown with their winners). Not loaded: the 34 local propositions and questions on the list.
local_coverage.s: Oklahoma State Election Board, NOVEMBER / 2026 List of Elections, and Candidates for Office 2026 (who filed for district attorney), and its official results of the June 16, 2026 Primary Election and the August 25, 2026 Runoff Primary Election; 26 O.S. 6-102 (an unopposed candidate is not printed on the ballot)

gaps.w: county officers who had no opponent
gaps.r: Oklahoma leaves an office off the ballot when only one candidate is left. A county seat settled in the June 16 primary or the August 25 runoff is shown with its winner, from the State Election Board's official results; a county officer who had no opponent in the primary or in November appears in no list or result, and the Board's filing portal, which lists who filed, refuses scripts, so those officers are not shown here.

gaps.w: city, town and school offices voted on June 16 or August 25
gaps.r: Coweta, Lawton, Mangum, Shawnee, Snyder, Tecumseh, Tulsa, Waynoka and Weatherford, the town of Inola and one school district held 22 contests for their own offices with the state's June 16 or August 25, 2026 elections, and none of those seats is on the November 3 ballot. The State Election Board's official results are read here only for a city contest whose top two are on the November ballot; whether each of these was a city's primary or its final election is set by its own charter, which this site has not read, so they are not shown.
